races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with proven C&D form, Jack Callan's claim valuable again after 27-day break
runners_data.comment: Three C&D wins; latest success at Wolverhampton under J Callan for first time; back up 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Three C&D wins but perhaps even more effective on Tapeta; had the benefit of Jack Callan's claim when successful at Wolverhampton (7f) last month and although back up 3lb he's perfectly capable of finding another race off this mark.

runners_data.name: Yehudi
runners_data.note: Prominent runner better on Polytrack than this surface, Billy Loughnane booking significant
runners_data.comment: Just two Polytrack runs, going close and winning over 7f at Kempton; likely contender
runners_data.spotlight: Has done most of his AW racing on Wolverhampton Tapeta but he's run his two best races on Kempton Polytrack (7f), going close in February and breaking his duck last month; back up 4lb; a likely contender on course debut.

runners_data.name: Francisco
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with C&D win for Charlie Tucker, fitted with tongue strap for tactical improvement
runners_data.comment: Two 7f handicap wins on AW, the latest over C&D in April; disappointing on turf here since
runners_data.spotlight: Two 7f handicap wins on the AW, the latest over C&D in April under Charlie Tucker, but he was disappointing on the turf track here (7f) since, given that he's handled that test in the past; shade to prove this time.

runners_data.name: Enpassant
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won last start at Southwell, 26-day gap should aid fitness for Jack Mitchell
runners_data.comment: Three 7f wins on AW elsewhere, the latest in April; lesser efforts in two starts since
runners_data.spotlight: Three 7f wins on AW elsewhere, most recently at Southwell in April; a quick return didn't pay off there next time and he was always behind when returned to turf at Leicester last month; has run well over C&D in the past, though, so he may be more himself this time.

runners_data.name: Fort Augustus
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong recent Southwell form, headgear and 14-day turnaround both positive
runners_data.comment: Won 2 of last 3 starts at Southwell since these aids fitted; acts on Polytrack; drawn wide
runners_data.spotlight: Won two of last three at Southwell (7f) since these aids were fitted, a steady late surge taking him to the front close home 14 days ago; acts on Polytrack, too, but plenty needs to go right today from a wide draw.

runners_data.name: Majestic Wave
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 51-day break after poor recent form, needs career-best revival
runners_data.comment: Disappointing run of form since good yard debut here; dropped a long way in the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Won 6f maiden at Navan as 2yo; promising yard debut over 6f on this track in February 2025 but he's mostly struggled since, thus the drop of 24lb in the weights since racing in Britain; should come on for his April reappearance and is one to keep an eye on for signs of a revival.

runners_data.name: Dashing Donkey
runners_data.note: Prominent runner winless on AW but handles surface, 54-day break a fitness concern for Marco Ghiani
runners_data.comment: All four wins front-running on turf, at 7f and 1m; 0-9 on AW but acts on Polytrack
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins from the front on turf, over 7f in 2024 and twice over 1m at Newmarket last summer; 0-9 on AW but he handles this surface and is not a forlorn hope on the return to 7f.

runners_data.name: Secret Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won here for previous yard but form declined badly, 3-day turnaround very quick
runners_data.comment: Has won at 6f, 7f and 1m for different yards this year but well below best on last 3 runs
runners_data.spotlight: Won at 6f and over C&D for James Owen at the start of the year, then over 1m here on yard debut in March, but his last three runs have been nothing like as good; has plenty to prove back at 7f.

runners_data.name: Adelaide Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong AW record, lowest weight compensates for recent poor form under De Sousa
runners_data.comment: Three 7f AW wins in 2025; 6lb lower than latest; close second back with former yard in May
runners_data.spotlight: Three 7f wins on Polytrack and Tapeta between April and June in 2025 for this yard; right out of luck for different trainers from November onwards but he fell a long way in the weights and shot home to take a late second at Southwell (7f) 14 days ago; should make hay off current mark, 6lb lower than latest win, if overcoming a wide draw.

runners_data.name: Oberon Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 78-day layoff with poor recent form, needs significant improvement for Finley Marsh
runners_data.comment: Signs of 7f ability on Tapeta; well beaten and bled from nose on yard debut in March
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of ability over 7f on Newcastle Tapeta but failed to stay 1m on handicap debut at Wetherby in April 2025; wasn't seen again until well beaten on Kempton AW (6f) in March for new yard, where he bled from the nose; best watched for now.

runners_data.name: Twitch
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who often leads but couldn't maintain effort recently, low weight helps Georgia Dobie
runners_data.comment: Often leads; tight with Francisco on C&D form in April but this looks more competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Often leads; tight between him and Francisco on C&D form in April but he couldn't hold his place on the turf track here since and this looks competitive, especially with others in the field who like to lead.

runners_data.name: Harbour Vision
runners_data.note: Front runner with exceptional AW record but 55-day break and age concerns, fitted with blinkers for sharpness
runners_data.comment: Last 11 wins on Tapeta; has gone off the boil of late; first Polytrack run for a year
runners_data.spotlight: Tremendous win record on AW, successful 16 times; however, the last 11 have been at Wolverhampton and he's gone off the boil since winning two in a row there (7f) at the start of the year; has it to prove in first Polytrack run for over a year.

races.paceDynamic: Harbour Vision is the sole confirmed front runner but carries warning flags about fading in the finish after 55 days off. Yehudi, Dashing Donkey and Twitch can press forward early, creating a moderate pace that shouldn't be overly testing through the middle stages. The lack of genuine early speed with stamina means this sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses who can position off the pace and finish strongly. This race shape strongly favours the late-running brigade who can exploit what should be a soft pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Harbour Vision sets modest fractions or fades as expected
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too slow for the prominent runners to sustain their kicks, allowing the patient hold-up horses to unleash finishing bursts. Split Elevens, Fort Augustus and Adelaide Bay can all capitalize on superior late speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners capitalize
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi and Dashing Donkey press Harbour Vision into honest fractions
scenarios.body: The moderate but steady pace suits horses who can track the leaders and kick when the front runner weakens. Yehudi's Polytrack form and Dashing Donkey's tactical speed become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Harbour Vision stays strong
scenarios.trigger: If the 11-year-old reproduces his peak AW form despite the layoff concerns
scenarios.body: His class and course knowledge overcome the fitness doubts, making the most of uncontested early fractions. The lack of pace pressure allows him to dictate and sustain his effort to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If Harbour Vision goes too slow early with minimal pressure from behind
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where positioning and jockey timing matter most than running style. The lightest weighted runners and strongest finishers can overcome poor tactical positions.

watchPoints.text: Harbour Vision could set crawling fractions if unopposed early, turning this into pure sprint finish
Yehudi and Dashing Donkey must commit to pressing the pace or the hold-up horses gain decisive advantage
Split Elevens and Fort Augustus both excel when getting patient rides in slowly-run races like this projects
Adelaide Bay carries just 124lbs but needs the pace to develop properly for De Sousa's late charge
Francisco and Secret Road both have C&D wins but return under different tactical circumstances than previous success

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap

runners_data.name: Peregrine Falcon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Billy Loughnane partnership clicking, but remains a maiden after 14 attempts despite consistent placings
runners_data.comment: 0-14 but involved in three tight finishes over 5f on Tapeta; first Polytrack run
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden after 14 runs, five under Billy Loughnane, but has been involved in tight finishes over 5f on Tapeta on three occasions so ought to find a race at some stage and perhaps this first go on Polytrack will suit.

runners_data.name: Shalaa Asker
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong course record, three recent wins show he's in good heart despite flat Southwell effort last time
runners_data.comment: Been busy; many good runs at 5f over the winter include three 5f wins; below best latest
runners_data.spotlight: Busy since the autumn; some narrow defeats to go with three 5f wins, on Polytrack elsewhere and Tapeta; ran flat at Southwell recently but he's realistically weighted if that wasn't a sign that he's going off the boil.

runners_data.name: Balon d'Or
runners_data.note: Hold-up type better on turf than AW, 45-day break and 9lb drop in weights since joining new yard could spark improvement
runners_data.comment: Mostly well held here for new yard but down 9lb since November; glimmer of revival latest
runners_data.spotlight: Both handicap wins on turf at Chester (5f and 6f); no great shakes on this track for new yard since November but he's dropped 9lb in that time and there was the glimmer of a revival here last time when back from a break; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: Front-running maiden who needs to settle better, recent hood experiment failed but Silvestre De Sousa booking suggests confidence
runners_data.comment: Maiden; two poor efforts of late but worth another go at 5f; now blinkered
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden; two poor efforts of late, with and without a hood, but he ran well for a long way behind a subsequent winner at Wolverhampton (6f) in April and is worth another go at 5f; first-time blinkers today.

runners_data.name: Diamond Dreamer
runners_data.note: Course winner who almost ended losing run here in March, hold-up style suits when pace is strong enough for finishing kick
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; came close to ending a losing AW run here (5f) in March; first C&D run since
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner who came close to ending a losing AW run when a fast-closing runner-up here (5f) in March (5f); returns to this C&D for the first time since and ought to go well if the race falls his way.

runners_data.name: Desdemona
runners_data.note: Tough hold-up filly with two spring wins, form tailed off recently but course victory shows she handles the track well
runners_data.comment: Two 5f wins in early spring, over C&D and at Chelmsford; had excuses since; form claims
runners_data.spotlight: Tough filly who took time to find her form again but won two in a row in early spring, over C&D (overcame a wide draw) and at Chelmsford (5f), and subsequent defeats came over 6f then very slowly away here in April; form claims.

runners_data.name: Honour Your Dreams
runners_data.note: Prominent type with six turf wins but woeful 0-22 AW record, weight advantage may not overcome surface concerns
runners_data.comment: Six turf wins; weights pull with Desdemona on C&D form in February but now 0-22 on AW
runners_data.spotlight: Six turf wins, three in 2025; 0-22 on AW and although having a healthy pull at the weights with Desdemona on their C&D run in February he's not looked in peak form on last two starts.

races.paceDynamic: Style King and Honour Your Dreams will press forward early, with Peregrine Falcon likely tracking just behind this duo in the opening stages. The pace should be reasonable but not frantic over this minimum distance, as Style King has shown he can sustain his effort when allowed to bowl along in front. The hold-up horses - Shalaa Asker, Diamond Dreamer, Desdemona and Balon d'Or - will need the pace to be strong enough to set up their finishing kicks. This race shape favours prominent racers and those able to travel strongly in the first half of the field, as they can position close enough to strike while avoiding traffic problems that often snare the hold-up brigade over this sharp 5f trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Style King or Peregrine Falcon can secure ideal positions tracking the pace without being bustled early.
scenarios.body: The winner can travel smoothly into contention and has the tactical speed to strike in the final furlong without relying on gaps opening late. This profile gets first run on the hold-up horses who need more time to wind up their challenges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough and the prominent horses come back to the field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Diamond Dreamer or Shalaa Asker can produce their best finishing kick to collar the leaders close home. Their proven course form and ability to quicken sharply becomes decisive when others tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Style King gets his own way in front with Honour Your Dreams tracking and no strong early pressure applied.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too slow for the hold-up horses to make up ground and the race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole. Style King can sustain his effort better than most when not pressured early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the market principles get their tactics wrong or fail to handle the track conditions properly.
scenarios.body: Balon d'Or shows his Chester form was no fluke and his 9lb drop in the weights proves decisive with better positioning. His proven turf ability gives him an edge if others struggle to adapt to the surface switch.

watchPoints.text: Style King dictating terms in front unchallenged - his stamina limitations become less relevant if allowed to control the gallop
Shalaa Asker's position turning for home - needs to be within striking distance to unleash his proven finishing kick
Diamond Dreamer getting a clear run in the straight - course specialist who showed renewed vigour when runner-up here in March
Honour Your Dreams adapting to the all-weather surface - perfect turf record but never won on artificial in 22 attempts
Peregrine Falcon's early positioning with Loughnane - needs to be prominent enough to avoid traffic but not waste energy racing keenly

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 'Confined' EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (2 Runs Or Less) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Sunshine Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with class edge through Gosden training and Oaks winner family connection, but needs to bounce back from disappointing favorite defeat
runners_data.comment: Well-bred filly; only sixth when odds-on at Sandown but this race looks much easier
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to connections' Oaks winner Soul Sister; close second to useful rival at Kempton (1m, AW) on sole 2yo start; managed only sixth when odds-on favourite for good Sandown novice (1m2f, good) in April but this race looks much easier and the return to Polytrack will suit; good chance.

runners_data.name: Kashooda
runners_data.note: Balding newcomer with strong French breeding including Listed-class siblings, complete unknown but dangerous on debut
runners_data.comment: Well-bred filly from a good stable; market helpful on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth foal; sister to French 7f 2yo/9.7f winner Khadidja, half-sister to three winners including Kawida (7f/1m 2yo including Listed; RPR 106) and Khinjani (1m2f; 94); dam 9.4f winner (68), half-sister to Australian 1m1f/1m2f Group 1 winner Zaaki; in good hands; market may guide on debut.

runners_data.name: Northern Bea
runners_data.note: Another newcomer with quality pedigree including 1m4f winner relation, Ward stable in poor form but breeding suggests ability
runners_data.comment: Closely related to a useful 1m4f winner; makes debut in race lacking strength in debut
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000gns yearling; eighth foal; closely related to 1m4f winner Royal Associate (RPR 99), half-sister to three winners including Kingfisher King (1m2f; 106) and Officer Of State (1m7f; 103); dam unplaced 1m-1m2f in France; makes debut in a race lacking strength in depth.

runners_data.name: Lightning Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who will get easy lead, consistent frame form and 14 days since last run ideal
runners_data.comment: Fair form when making the frame twice over 1m; holds each-way claims at least here
runners_data.spotlight: Fair form when making the frame on both starts this spring, more recently when third of 11 at Southwell (1m); holds each-way claims at least if suited by the longer trip here.

runners_data.name: Antiquarian
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who was flattered at Ascot in slowly-run race, needs significant pace improvement to be competitive
runners_data.comment: Flattered by proximity when sixth in slowly run Ascot contest last month
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled on 2yo debut (6f) and was almost certainly flattered by proximity to principals when sixth of seven in slowly run contest at Ascot (1m2f, good) last month.

runners_data.name: Shopaholic
runners_data.note: Older filly carrying penalty, showed promise over course and distance on debut but others preferred
runners_data.comment: Made fairly encouraging debut over C&D; ground a possible excuse last time
runners_data.spotlight: Made fairly encouraging debut when fifth of eight over C&D in April and may not have been suited by good to soft turf when below that form last month but others in this line-up look stronger.

runners_data.name: Arrivera
runners_data.note: Long absence since disappointing debut, needs major improvement to feature despite trainer's decent recent form
runners_data.comment: Showed only a glimmer of promise on debut at Southwell (1m) on New Year's Day
runners_data.spotlight: First foal from a useful 7f AW winner; showed only a glimmer of promise before weakening into sixth of seven on debut at Southwell (1m) on New Year's Day.

runners_data.name: Coral Cathedral
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who was too green on debut, long absence and trainer struggling for winners
runners_data.comment: Too green to do herself justice when 33-1 for debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in December
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a German Group 3 winner; too green to do herself justice when 33-1 for debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in December; needs to have made good progress in the meantime.

runners_data.name: Musical Accord
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who failed to fire at Wolverhampton last time, needs to recapture debut Newbury promise
runners_data.comment: Midfield in good Newbury maiden in April but last month's AW run was a backward step
runners_data.spotlight: Midfield in fairly good Newbury maiden (1m2f, good) on debut in April but unable to land any sort of blow at Wolverhampton (9.4f) last month; needs to up her game here.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who was never competitive on debut, 100-1 chance suggests stable confidence lacking
runners_data.comment: Always behind when 100-1 for recent debut at Southwell (1m)
runners_data.spotlight: Has a good pedigree but was always behind when 100-1 for recent debut at Southwell (1m).

runners_data.name: Kenkelly
runners_data.note: Unknown style but was well-held in small field at Yarmouth, hard to fancy on that evidence
runners_data.comment: Didn't achieve a great deal when third of five on debut; soundly beaten since
runners_data.spotlight: Probably didn't achieve a great deal when well-held third of five in race won easily by short-odds favourite at Yarmouth (11.5f, good to firm) in April and was soundly beaten when dropped to 1m2f at Goodwood last month.

runners_data.name: Hunting Berries
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with terrible form figures, completely outclassed at this level
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at triple-digit odds on first two starts (6f/1m); upped in trip again here
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at triple-digit odds on first two starts (6f/1m); upped in trip again here.

runners_data.name: Corallience
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who suffered heavy defeat behind Sunshine Star last time, needs significant turnaround
runners_data.comment: Not disgraced on 2yo debut but suffered heavy defeat on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced on 2yo debut at Newbury (1m, soft) but suffered heavy defeat when reappearing at Sandown (1m2f, good; behind Sunshine Star) six weeks ago.

races.paceDynamic: Lightning Glory will lead from the gates with her confirmed front-running style, likely getting an easy time of it with no other obvious pace pressers in this field. The vast majority of runners are hold-up types (Antiquarian, Musical Accord, Blue Tulip, Hunting Berries, Corallience) or unknown quantities (Kashooda, Northern Bea, Arrivera, Shopaholic, Kenkelly), meaning Lightning Glory can dictate fractions without pressure. Only Sunshine Star shows prominent tendencies to potentially track the leader, but even she's more tactical than aggressive. This sets up perfectly for horses with early pace who can position close to Lightning Glory, as the weak tempo will leave plenty in reserve for the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lightning Glory Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lightning Glory gets the expected soft lead and maintains her recent form improvement
scenarios.body: She can dictate comfortable fractions and has enough in hand to resist challers, having shown consistent frame-hitting form at this level. The weak pace plays directly into her hands as the main pace angle in a field full of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sunshine Star tracks Lightning Glory closely and the two prominent runners control the race
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace from others allows these two to set it up perfectly between them, with Sunshine Star's superior class telling. Her connections with the Gosdens and half-sister relation to Oaks winner gives her the quality edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomers Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If either Kashooda or Northern Bea show significant improvement from their breeding and connections
scenarios.body: The Balding/Ward newcomers have strong pedigrees and could exploit the weak pace if debuting with serious intent. Their unknown quantities status makes them dangerous if ready to go.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes even slower than expected and hold-up horses can close strongly
scenarios.body: Musical Accord or Corallience could benefit from a crawling pace that sets up their late-running styles. However, they'd need significant improvement from recent disappointing efforts to capitalize.

watchPoints.text: Lightning Glory's early fractions will determine the entire race shape - if she gets too soft a lead she becomes very dangerous
Sunshine Star's position tracking the leader is crucial as she has the class to win but needs to overcome recent poor form
Watch for any market support for newcomers Kashooda or Northern Bea as connections may know more than form suggests
Musical Accord's early position will indicate if Beckett thinks she can improve on recent disappointing efforts
The general pace through the opening half-mile will expose whether this becomes a sprint finish or staying test

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaori
runners_data.note: Returns from 255-day break but prominent style suits this race shape with controlled pace expected.
runners_data.comment: Placed in 7f maiden in September; open to improvement in middle-distance handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Made the frame on all three 2yo starts, most notably when third of 12 in Leicester maiden (7f, good to soft) in September; makes handicap/AW debut after 255-day absence but has plenty of scope for improvement in middle-distance handicaps this year.

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage with limited early pace, though step up to 1m2f should help.
runners_data.comment: Three good runs over 1m this season; needs to find a bit more over this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Three good runs over 1m this year, the latest in refitted blinkers at Kempton four weeks ago, but probably needs this longer trip to unlock some improvement.

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Front-runner gets dream scenario as sole pace-setter, can dictate fractions without pressure.
runners_data.comment: Dominated small field from the front last month and is now 3-6 for new stable this year
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner with 3-6 strike-rate for new stable this year, the latest win gained in four-runner contest at Wolverhampton (9.4f) last month; enjoyed the run of the race that day and has gone up another 6lb but is evidently in excellent nick.

runners_data.name: Extraterrestrial
runners_data.note: Prominent racer ideally positioned to track uncontested leader, but must handle AW surface better than last turf run.
runners_data.comment: Below form last time (raced too freely) but in the mix if quickly back on song
runners_data.spotlight: Well down the field after racing too freely on turf last month but was in good form beforehand, most notably when close second at Southwell (1m3f; first-time cheekpieces) two runs ago; in the mix if back on song.

runners_data.name: Raspoutine
runners_data.note: Won here over 1m in April and prominent style perfectly suits this tactical setup with step up in trip.
runners_data.comment: Course winner on seasonal/handicap debut and another two good runs since; blinkers on
runners_data.spotlight: Won in good style here (1m) on seasonal/handicap debut in April and made the frame on both starts since, more recently when upped to 1m2f at Salisbury 12 days ago; returns to this track with first-time blinkers fitted; may still have more improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Central Command
runners_data.note: Hold-up style poorly suited to limited early pace despite recent Newcastle win over this distance.
runners_data.comment: Flopped badly on turf last time but was emphatic winner on seasonal/handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Needs to bounce back quickly from very disappointing turf debut at Haydock a fortnight ago but came from off the pace for emphatic win at Newcastle (1m2f) on seasonal/handicap debut in early May, and has obvious claims if judged on that performance.

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Express will break and lead as the sole confirmed front-runner, setting a controlled tempo with no early pressure in this small field. Kaori, Booziebrunch, Raspoutine and Extraterrestrial will settle in a mid-pack cluster behind the leader, while Central Command drops out the back as the designated hold-up horse. The lack of pace pressure means Lexington Express can dictate fractions and potentially steal a march turning for home. This race shape heavily favours the leader and prominent racers who can track the pace, as there's insufficient early speed to set up a strong finish for closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express maintains his recent front-running form and dictates moderate fractions.
scenarios.body: The leader gets an easy time of it and proves hard to peg back, while prominent racers like Raspoutine and Extraterrestrial benefit from the honest tempo but can't quite get past. The lack of early pace means no serious collapse from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers can improve past the leader in the straight without the pace collapsing.
scenarios.body: Raspoutine or Extraterrestrial get the perfect trip tracking the uncontested leader and have enough left to strike in the final furlong. The moderate pace suits their style perfectly as they don't have to come from too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes slower than expected and Central Command gets the strong finish he needs.
scenarios.body: The tempo becomes pedestrian enough for Central Command to unleash his preferred late kick, despite the tactical disadvantage of the race shape. His recent Newcastle win shows he has the ability when things fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Gets Into Mix
scenarios.trigger: If Kaori's 255-day absence proves no hindrance and benefits from the race shape.
scenarios.body: The Boughey newcomer shows improved form on handicap debut and the prominent style suits the race perfectly. The long absence becomes irrelevant if the ability is there.

watchPoints.text: Lexington Express gets uncontested lead and proves impossible to peg back with soft fractions
Central Command struggles to get competitive from the back with insufficient pace to close into
Extraterrestrial repeats free-running antics from last turf start and wastes energy early
Kaori shows no signs of rustiness despite 255-day absence on handicap debut
Raspoutine handles step back up to 1m2f after good Lingfield form at shorter trips

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Diamondinthedark
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 187-day break with winning form at this surface but may need the run.
runners_data.comment: Off the mark on her second start, at Wolverhampton in November; handicap debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark on her second start, at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in November; steps up in trip on handicap debut on first run since and may well show improvement; market will be best guide.

runners_data.name: Doodling
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but form has declined since promising Kempton second, headgear change suggests issues.
runners_data.comment: 0-4 but was only beaten a neck at Kempton in April; two lesser runs since.

races.paceDynamic: Hamaleel will take them along as the sole confirmed front-runner, but won't be pressured early allowing her to dictate a sustainable tempo. The real drama develops 2-3 furlongs out when Diamondinthedark, Doodling, Polka Blue, and Bella Bisbee all converge from prominent positions, creating serious traffic problems. Behind them, Sahana, Pretty Danielle, Ritaal, and Startled Lady face the classic hold-up runners' nightmare of finding clear passage through the inevitable squeeze. This race shape heavily favours prominent racers who can position just off the pace and avoid the late scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet can secure good positions without early scrimmaging
scenarios.body: The traffic jam behind allows the early positioned horses to kick clear while hold-up runners get shuffled back. Polka Blue's recent win and Bella Bisbee's course form shine through when it matters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up Hero Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If one of the back-markers gets a dream run through late
scenarios.body: Sahana's proven course form or Pretty Danielle's consistency pays off when they thread through the needle. The pace setters and prominent runners have done too much work up front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hamaleel Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner maintains her gallop to the line despite pressure
scenarios.body: Her sustainable early pace leaves enough in reserve to repel the challengers, especially with the prominent runners getting in each other's way. Watson's tactics prove perfect for the track configuration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes major interference and fallers benefit
scenarios.body: An unfancied runner like Startled Lady or Ritaal profits from the carnage ahead, getting through on the rails or widest of all. Form gets thrown out the window in a rough-run affair.

watchPoints.text: Hamaleel's stamina reserves as she steps up in trip with only one 7f+ win from eight attempts.
Traffic congestion between Doodling, Polka Blue, Bella Bisbee and Diamondinthedark turning for home.
Sahana and Pretty Danielle getting clear runs from the back as the field bunches approaching the furlong pole.
Kieran O'Neill's positioning of Bella Bisbee early to avoid her usual tendency to get outpaced.
Whether Ritaal shows any sharpness returning from the break under new connections.

races.paceDynamic: Forest Berry is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should have an uncontested lead through moderate fractions. Ron's Angel and Sea Of Sardinia will sit prominent but neither appears keen to take on Forest Berry early. The lack of genuine pace pressure means Forest Berry can dictate comfortable splits before kicking clear in the straight. This tactical setup heavily favors front runners and prominent racers who can track the leader without pressure, while hold-up horses like Deja Vu Diva and Last Dandelion will struggle to make up ground against a sustainable tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forest Berry Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Forest Berry gets an easy lead and dictates her own fractions
scenarios.body: She can steal a march turning for home with no serious pace pressure, maintaining her stamina reserves for a sustained drive. The lack of early pressure allows her superior form (RPR 72) to shine through against this modest field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ron's Angel or Sea Of Sardinia can stalk Forest Berry without racing keenly
scenarios.body: They benefit from the moderate pace by staying within striking distance before quickening past the leader in the final furlong. Ron's Angel's strong Bath debut form makes her the most likely beneficiary of this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debut Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the newcomers (Potters Margot, Zigazig Ah, Clear Horizon) shows significant improvement from home
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows them to settle and finish strongly despite their inexperience. Zigazig Ah's pedigree and Saffie Osborne booking suggest she could be the pick of the debutants.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and collapses in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Last Dandelion or Deja Vu Diva can use their hold-up style to sweep past tired leaders. Last Dandelion showed some ability at Newmarket and could benefit from a stronger pace collapse scenario.

Last Dandelion breaks slowly again as she did on debut and gives herself too much to do from rear

races.paceDynamic: Case Study will set the early pace with Lordsbridge Bay and Moonlight Angel tracking close behind, creating a measured gallop over this mile trip on standard going. The pace should be sustainable rather than frantic, with the main body of hold-up horses including Sail On Sailor, Fallacious Promise, and Beryl's Girl settling in behind the leaders. This sets up a tactical affair where the prominently-raced horses can dictate terms without excessive pressure, before the hold-up brigade mount their challenges in the final three furlongs. The race shape clearly favors prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace without getting involved in early battles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Case Study and Lordsbridge Bay can maintain a steady gallop without being pressured early.
scenarios.body: The front division controls the race throughout, with Case Study benefiting from first-time cheekpieces and Lordsbridge Bay getting the step up in trip he needs. The hold-up horses find too much to do when the pace quickens approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too slow and the race develops into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses get the perfect setup as the leaders crawl early, allowing Sail On Sailor and Fallacious Promise to unleash their finishing kicks. Both have shown they can win when getting the right tactical scenario and this trip suits their profiles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Case Study goes too fast early and the front-runners tire dramatically.
scenarios.body: The sustainable pace becomes unsustainable as Case Study overdoes it in front, creating opportunities for mid-division horses like Beryl's Girl making her AW debut. Horses that can adapt tactically in-running benefit from the changing race dynamic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Intervention
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders underperform and the race opens up for a surprise result.
scenarios.body: The higher-rated horses fail to fire, allowing an improver like Angel Summer to benefit from the step up in trip despite her turf concerns. Long absent runners finding their form create unexpected results in a wide-open finish.

watchPoints.text: Case Study could set too strong an early pace in first-time cheekpieces, potentially compromising his and other front-runners' chances.
Hove Ranger returns after 99 days off and may need the run despite his previous encouraging AW form at this course and distance.
Sail On Sailor's last win came from tracking the pace before leading late, watch if he can get the same tactical position here.
Several runners including Laurasia and Mist Of Time return after very long absences and may struggle with race fitness.
Beryl's Girl makes her AW debut having raced only on turf, watch how she handles the surface switch in her first handicap.
